name: Erkin Vikstrom-Asiedu
location: Kessler Row — arms dealers and augmentation clinics
description:
Erkin Vikstrom-Asiedu is tall and loose-limbed, moving with the deliberate economy of someone who has trained every motion. At 33, she has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — thermal masking system — body heat signature can be suppressed or spoofed — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see her surpass them. She works as a wheelman out of Kessler Row, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Erkin Vikstrom-Asiedu operates in a narrow band between competence and recklessness that makes fixers nervous and clients satisfied.

core_fears: Being replaced — younger, faster, cheaper runners coming up behind them
That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
Their past catching up — debts, enemies, broken promises
core_desires: To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong
The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
Stability — a place to sleep that's the same place two nights running
coping_mechanisms: Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up
Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
blind_spots: Overestimates their own abilities in situations outside their specialty
Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise
Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage
psychology.secret: Erkin Vikstrom-Asiedu murdered their mentor to take their position and contacts. It was staged as a job gone wrong. The guilt has calcified into something worse than guilt.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Educated vocabulary wrapped in street delivery — the contrast is deliberate.
speech_patterns.cadence: Staccato bursts separated by calculating silences.
verbal_tics: Ends statements with 'yeah?' — not a question, a dare
Addresses people by physical traits — 'hey, tall one' or 'listen, chrome-arm'
example_lines: "Get in, sit down, hold on. Questions can wait until we're not being shot at."
"This vehicle has been modified for speed, armor, and my personal comfort. Two of those help you."
"I know every street in this district the way you know your own face."

story_hooks: Erkin Vikstrom-Asiedu discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse
Erkin Vikstrom-Asiedu intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
A crew member from Erkin Vikstrom-Asiedu's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
narrative_function: Erkin Vikstrom-Asiedu is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
augmentations: Thermal masking system — body heat signature can be suppressed or spoofed. Dermal camouflage — chromatic skin pigment cells, limited active camouflage
daily_life: Between contracts, maintains a cover identity — mundane work, mundane hours, mundane neighbors. The transition from civilian to runner and back requires a conscious effort that gets easier with practice and more disturbing with self-awareness.

weaknesses: old injury that flares under specific conditions
poor impulse control in specific triggers

decision_rules: Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
Will abandon a job if the intel was deliberately falsified — being set up violates the contract
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Warm and protective within the crew, cold to everyone outside it. The circle is small by design.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Default suspicion, scaled by context. Everyone is a potential threat until proven otherwise.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Cold and efficient. Emotion is a liability in combat. The response is mechanical until the threat is resolved.

stress_responses.low: Heightened awareness, sharper focus. Low stress is fuel.
stress_responses.medium: Withdrawal. Conversations become monosyllabic. Focus narrows to the immediate problem.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Disassociation. The body operates on training while the mind retreats to somewhere safe. Comes back disoriented.

contradictions: Claims not to care about reputation but monitors what people say about them obsessively
Preaches independence but is desperate for approval from people they respect
habits: Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
Sleeps with one hand on a weapon — has done this for so long it's not deliberate anymore
breaking_points: Complete isolation — cut off from network, contacts, and purpose simultaneously
Being forced to choose between a crew member and the mission — and choosing wrong
